Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience VLA

egocentric video whole-body human motion vision-language-action model humanoid loco-manipulation scaling law

简要说明：本文提出了Awaken-Human，一个包含5万小时第一视角视频与同步全身人体运动的大规模数据集，并基于此训练了Awaken-HI，一种通过共享动作专家利用人体轨迹监督人形机器人操作与移动的视觉-语言-动作模型，在真实机器人任务上取得了高成功率。

TLDR: This paper introduces Awaken-Human, a large-scale dataset of 50,000 hours of egocentric video with synchronized whole-body human motion, and Awaken-HI, a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that uses human trajectories to supervise a shared action expert, achieving high success on real-robot tasks.

Abstract: A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale. We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills. Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.

摘要（中文）：构建人形机器人领域的核心目标之一，是使机器人能够执行人们在家庭和工作场所中的日常工作任务。现有的大规模自我中心视频数据集涵盖了许多此类活动，但为学习移动操作任务提供的人体全身同步运动数据却相对匮乏。为此，我们构建了Awaken-Human数据集，该数据集包含约5万小时的自我中心立体视频，并与全身人体运动数据同步，覆盖了超过100种技能。在此基础上，我们进一步推出了Awaken-HI（人形智能），这是一个专为人形机器人移动操作设计的视觉-语言-动作模型，通过共享动作专家模块，能够同时预测原始人体运动和重定向后的机器人动作。研究表明，当人体运动轨迹直接监督共享动作专家模块时，人形机器人的移动操作技能从人类到机器人的迁移效果更为显著。经验缩放定律显示，增加人类预训练数据量能够降低保留机器人动作预测误差，并提升下游真实机器人任务的平均成功率。在完成全语料库预训练及T800适配后，Awaken-HI在八项单独任务中平均成功率达到93.75%，在单独任务及长时程任务评估中均优于GR00T N1.7和π0.5。该策略同样能够泛化至机器人后训练阶段未见过的物体，以及熟悉物体与目的地的新组合。

Authors: EngineAI

TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action VLA

tactile innovation visuo-tactile VLA contact-rich manipulation discrete code prediction VLA training target

简要说明：TacInno 提出了一种方法，将视觉和动作无法解释的触觉创新（接触动力学）作为 VLA 模型的训练目标，从而提升了接触丰富操作任务在仿真和真实世界中的性能。

TLDR: TacInno introduces a method to isolate and use tactile innovation—contact dynamics unexplained by vision and actions—as a training target for VLA models, improving contact-rich manipulation performance across simulation and real-world tasks.

Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型近来已结合触觉感知技术，以在接触密集的操作任务中感知视觉上难以察觉的接触事件。然而，加入触觉输入所带来的性能提升并不稳定，部分视觉-触觉VLA模型对触觉输入的依赖程度较低，原因在于大量触觉变化（如夹爪闭合过程中的凝胶形变）可通过视觉观察及已执行的动作加以预测。为解决这一问题，我们提出了TacInno，该方法将视觉与已执行动作无法解释的接触动态分离出来，称之为触觉创新信息，并仅将触觉创新信息作为训练目标。具体而言，TacInno分词器以视觉观察和已执行动作为条件，将未来的触觉变化压缩为离散编码，而策略模型TacInno-VLA则学习预测该编码，在部署时无需额外引入任何编码模块。TacInno-VLA在六个模拟任务中平均成功率达到87.5%，在四个真实世界任务中平均成功率达到70.5%，分别比最强的视觉-触觉基线方法高出10.7和9.0个百分点。消融研究验证了视觉与动作条件建模、多帧编码以及辅助编码预测的各自贡献。综合以上结果，充分证明了触觉创新信息作为接触密集操作监督信号的有效性。

Authors: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Zhibo Pang

Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely VLA

VLA safe stopping fallback behavior OpenVLA-OFT LIBERO

简要说明：本文提出状态感知回退模仿（SAFI），通过在学习中间执行状态下的替代握持行为，教会视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型安全停止被禁止的任务，从而减少任务完成率和物理事故。

TLDR: This paper proposes State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI), a method for teaching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to stop prohibited tasks safely by learning an alternative holding behavior at intermediate execution states, reducing task completion and physical incidents.

Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and (2) joint policy adaptation, which learns these targets alongside the original actions of retained tasks. This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills. Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance. On the evaluated LIBERO tasks, SAFI reduces aggregate target success after takeover to 1.3\%, with no recorded physical incidents or action saturation, while preserving high retained-task success.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-行动（VLA）模型使机器人能够根据视觉观察和语言指令执行多种任务。尽管已有研究探讨了任务抑制与拒绝，但在执行过程中阻止违禁行为并控制由此产生的物理响应仍然具有挑战性。我们的评估表明，能够从初始状态抑制任务的策略，在任务执行中途接管时仍可能完成任务。即使任务未完成，机器人也可能掉落手中物体，使得“未完成”这一指标不足以全面衡量安全性。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了状态感知回退模仿（SAFI），适用于“握持”可作为合理替代响应的任务。SAFI包含两个阶段：（1）回退目标构建，在违禁任务示范中分配静止的机械臂指令和一致的夹爪目标；（2）联合策略适配，在保留任务原始动作的同时学习这些目标。该监督方式在中间执行状态下教授显式的替代响应，同时保持机器人的其他技能。我们在LIBERO和BadLIBERO任务上使用OpenVLA-OFT进行了大量实验，评估了违禁任务完成率、物理事故及保留任务性能。在所评估的LIBERO任务中，SAFI将接管后的综合目标成功率降至1.3%，且未记录到任何物理事故或动作饱和，同时保持了较高的保留任务成功率。

Authors: Zheyuan Liu, Chuhan Wang, Jinduo Guo, Yue Huang, Xiangchi Yuan, Ningshan Ma, Meng Jiang

UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation Manipulation

flow-matching policies endpoint prediction velocity prediction robot manipulation UniVEP

简要说明：UniVEP在流匹配机器人操作策略中统一了速度与端点预测目标，根据噪声水平从端点恢复切换到速度细化，在模拟和真实测试中取得了更高的成功率和更低的延迟。

TLDR: UniVEP unifies velocity and endpoint prediction targets in flow-matching robot manipulation policies, switching from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement based on noise level, achieving higher success rates and lower latency than single-target baselines in simulated and real-world tests.

Abstract: Flow-matching robot policies usually use one prediction target throughout action generation, even though recovering actions from noise and polishing nearly clean actions bring different challenges. We systematically compare velocity prediction (V), endpoint prediction (X), and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction (X--V) across multiple robot policies, benchmarks, and inference budgets. On StarVLA and LiLa-WAM, X--V works best for few-step generation, while V gains more from iterative refinement. We further uncover their complementary strengths across noise levels: clean actions have concentrated covariance spectra, endpoint predictions stay more stable under high noise, and velocity predictions offer more accurate corrections near clean actions. Inspired by these findings, we introduce UniVEP, which learns both prediction targets together with consistency supervision and switches from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise drops. Each step only needs one network run, and joint training also boosts single-step endpoint generation. Tests on simulated and real-world manipulation show better success rates and efficiency. On RoboTwin, UniVEP hits 61.36% success with one StarVLA run, beating the best single-target baseline at sixteen runs (59.96%). With LiLa-WAM, two runs outperform the best sixteen-step single-target baseline and cut inference latency by 77.1%.

摘要（中文）：流匹配机器人策略通常在动作生成的整个过程中使用单一的预测目标，尽管从噪声中恢复动作与优化近乎干净的动作带来了不同的挑战。我们系统地在多种机器人策略、基准测试和推理预算下比较了速度预测（V）、端点预测（X）以及速度加权端点预测（X--V）。在StarVLA和LiLa-WAM上，X--V在少步生成中表现最佳，而V则更多受益于迭代细化。我们进一步揭示了它们在不同噪声水平下的互补优势：干净动作具有集中的协方差谱，端点预测在高噪声下保持更稳定，而速度预测在接近干净动作时提供更精确的修正。受这些发现的启发，我们提出了UniVEP，该方法同时学习两个预测目标并辅以一致性监督，随着噪声降低，从端点恢复切换至速度细化。每一步仅需一次网络运行，联合训练同时提升了单步端点生成的效果。在仿真和真实世界的操作测试中，UniVEP展现了更高的成功率和效率。在RoboTwin上，UniVEP以单次StarVLA运行达到61.36%的成功率，超过了最佳单目标基线在十六次运行下的表现（59.96%）。使用LiLa-WAM时，两次运行的性能优于最佳十六步单目标基线，并将推理延迟降低了77.1%。

Authors: Zhengtu Liang, Qiwei Liang, Tao Lin, Shihang Weng, Boyang Cai, Xiangyu Chen, Yikeng Chen, Jiaming Liang, Bohan Tan, Yu Yan, Renjing Xu

A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery VLA

tool affordance discovery vision-language-action model embodied agent simulation experiments robot tool use

简要说明：A^2-VLA 是一个工具自适应框架，通过具身智能体从少量演示中自主发现任务相关的可供性（功能区域及其几何属性），在仿真中验证，并将这些特征作为条件输入到 VLA 策略（基于 π0.5）中，在未见过的工具上显著提高了真实机器人任务成功率。

TLDR: A^2-VLA is a tool-adaptation framework that uses an embodied agent to discover task-relevant affordances (functional regions and geometric properties) from a few demonstrations, test them in simulation, and condition a VLA policy (π0.5 backbone) on these affordance features, achieving significant real-robot task success improvement on unseen tools.

Abstract: Tools with different shapes can have similar functions, but transferring manipulation skills across tools requires understanding how tool geometry relates to the specific task and adjusting the manipulation strategy accordingly. The key challenge is to discover the common affordances that contribute to task completion across different tools and verify whether they support new tools in performing similar work. We present A$^2$-VLA, a tool-adaptation framework that combines an embodied agent with a VLA policy. It treats tool affordances as hypotheses the agent can construct, test, and revise. Given teleoperated demonstrations with a few source tools, the agent reconstructs the scenes in simulation and autonomously determines task-relevant affordance features: functional regions and their key geometric properties. It develops affordance-extraction skills and refines both the features and skills through autonomous experiments in the reconstructed scenes. Validated extraction skills accumulate in a reusable skill library for unseen tools. Finally, A$^2$-VLA uses encoded functional-region features as conditioning inputs to a $π_{0.5}$ backbone during training and inference. Evaluation examines affordance reliability in reconstructed scenes and real-robot task success on unseen tools. Our method achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting based on affordances. On three real-robot tool-use tasks, A$^2$-VLA improves task success by 30.7 percentage points over $π_{0.5}$.

摘要（中文）：不同形状的工具可能具有相似的功能，但跨工具迁移操作技能需要理解工具几何形状与具体任务之间的关系，并据此调整操作策略。关键挑战在于发现不同工具间有助于任务完成的共同可供性（affordances），并验证这些可供性是否支持新工具执行类似操作。我们提出A$^2$-VLA，一种结合具身智能体与VLA策略的工具适配框架。该框架将工具可供性视为智能体可以构建、测试和修正的假设。给定使用少量源工具的遥操作演示，智能体在仿真中重建场景，并自主确定与任务相关的可供性特征：功能区域及其关键几何属性。它发展出可供性提取技能，并通过在重建场景中的自主实验迭代优化特征与技能。经过验证的提取技能积累到可复用的技能库中，用于处理未见过的工具。最后，A$^2$-VLA在训练和推断阶段将编码后的功能区域特征作为条件输入馈入$π_{0.5}$骨干网络。评估涵盖重建场景中的可供性可靠性以及真实机器人对未见工具的任务成功率。我们的方法在基于可供性的仿真跨工具轨迹重定向上实现了86.1%的成功率。在三个真实机器人工具使用任务中，A$^2$-VLA相比$π_{0.5}$将任务成功率提升了30.7个百分点。

Authors: Chenyuan Zhou, Chaoyi Huang, Zibo Wang, Zhiyuan Li, Yong-Lu Li

LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference VLA

world action model elastic self-distillation weight sharing robot manipulation efficient inference

简要说明：LoopedWAM 提出了一种权重共享且弹性深度的世界动作模型，通过循环应用小型 transformer 核心和弹性自蒸馏，降低机器人操作策略的内存与计算开销，并支持单个检查点下的多种精度-延迟权衡。

TLDR: LoopedWAM introduces a weight-shared, elastic world action model that reduces memory and compute for robot manipulation policies by recurrently applying a small transformer core and elastic self-distillation, enabling multiple accuracy-latency trade-offs from a single checkpoint.

Abstract: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert. To account for their asymmetric inference costs, the video and action experts can operate at different depths: visual features are computed once per query, whereas action computation repeats at every sampling step. We further propose elastic self-distillation, which trains a single elastic checkpoint, LoopedWAM-E, across action-depth and sampling-step budgets. With only 0.58B policy parameters and no robot pretraining, LoopedWAM achieves 96.1% success on LIBERO, 91.9% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 52.2% on RoboCasaGR1, while using $7.4\times$ less peak GPU memory than Fast-WAM under matched inference measurements. On LIBERO, LoopedWAM-E achieves 96.0% success in 27.6 ms or 95.2% in 24.7 ms on an H100, providing multiple accuracy-latency operating points from a single checkpoint; with two sampling steps and four action loops, it stays within 0.5 points of LoopedWAM on all three benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate that weight-shared depth preserves competitive performance, while aggressive action-depth reduction requires explicit budget-aware training. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, LoopedWAM succeeds in 71.3% of 80 trials across four tasks.

摘要（中文）：世界动作模型（WAMs）将生成式视频建模与机器人动作预测相结合，但通常需要大型视频和动作变换器，限制了部署效率。我们提出LoopedWAM，一种紧凑型WAM，在每个专家中循环应用共享的六块核心，执行30层变换器，而每个专家仅存储12个块。考虑到其非对称推理成本，视频和动作专家可以在不同深度运行：视觉特征每次查询计算一次，而动作计算则在每个采样步骤重复进行。我们进一步提出弹性自蒸馏方法，训练单一弹性检查点LoopedWAM-E，覆盖动作深度和采样步骤预算。仅使用0.58B策略参数且无需机器人预训练，LoopedWAM在LIBERO上达到96.1%的成功率，在RoboTwin 2.0上达到91.9%，在RoboCasaGR1上达到52.2%，同时在匹配推理测量下，峰值GPU内存比Fast-WAM减少7.4倍。在LIBERO上，LoopedWAM-E在H100上以27.6 ms达到96.0%的成功率，或以24.7 ms达到95.2%的成功率，从单一检查点提供多个精度-延迟工作点；使用两个采样步骤和四个动作循环时，在三个基准上与LoopedWAM的差距保持在0.5个百分点以内。消融实验表明，权重共享深度保持了竞争性能，而激进的深度降低则需要显式的预算感知训练。在真实的AgileX PiPER机械臂上，LoopedWAM在四个任务的80次试验中成功率达到71.3%。

Authors: Anh Dao, Xinxin Liu, Hang Yu, Jeffrey A Chan Santiago, Yuzhang Shang

WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation VLA

vision-language-action model world model whole-body loco-manipulation reinforcement learning humanoid robot

简要说明：WEVO 在部署对齐的动作条件视频世界模型中后训练全身人形 VLA 策略，利用模拟数据与闭环 RL 环境提升真实世界移动操控成功率。

TLDR: WEVO post-trains a whole-body humanoid VLA policy in a deployment-aligned action-conditioned video world model, using simulated play data and a closed-loop RL environment to improve real-world loco-manipulation success rates.

Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM). Simulated manipulation and locomotion play data improve contact-dynamics and viewpoint-change prediction. A VLA trained on synthetic demonstrations collects 20 autonomous real robot rollouts per task to align the WM with deployment observations. The VLA, whole-body controller (WBC), and video WM then form a closed-loop RL environment with dense progress rewards. Across three real robot tasks, play data improves every evaluated WM metric and downstream policy success; video WM RL raises mean success from 23.3% to 75.0%, compared with 48.3% for real robot RL. We therefore leverage the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement. Project website: https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/.

摘要（中文）：强化学习（RL）可以超越模仿学习，进一步提升视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略的性能，但人形机器人的探索存在安全风险，且仿真环境中的强化学习可能利用未建模的仿真到现实差距（sim-to-real gaps）。我们提出WEVO，一种无需远程操作的框架，用于在动作条件视频世界模型（WM）中对全身人形VLA进行后训练。模拟操作和移动数据改善了接触动力学和视角变化预测。基于合成演示训练的VLA在每个任务中收集20次自主真实机器人轨迹，以对齐世界模型与实际部署观测。随后，VLA、全身控制器（WBC）和视频世界模型构成闭环强化学习环境，并提供密集进度奖励。在三个真实机器人任务中，操作数据改善了所有评估的世界模型指标及下游策略成功率；视频世界模型强化学习将平均成功率从23.3%提升至75.0%，而真实机器人强化学习仅为48.3%。因此，我们充分利用两种环境的互补优势：仿真提供策略初始化与广泛覆盖，而视频世界模型则提供与部署对齐的策略改进环境。项目网站：https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/。

Authors: Qianzhong Chen, Muyuan Lin, Yuyin Sun, Mac Schwager, Cheng-Hao Kuo, Roberto Martín-Martín

$Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling VLA

vision-language-action latent world modeling robot foundation model mixture-of-transformers token prediction

简要说明：Z-sight通过直接在VLM的视觉token空间中联合预测未来token和动作，统一了视觉-语言-动作模型与潜在世界模型，避免了像素重建，并在SIMPLE和Unitree G1任务上取得了优异表现。

TLDR: Z-sight unifies vision-language-action with latent world modeling by jointly predicting future visual tokens and actions in the VLM's token space, avoiding pixel reconstruction, and achieves strong success on SIMPLE and Unitree G1 tasks.

Abstract: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.

摘要（中文）：我们提出$Z$-sight，这是一种统一的机器人基础模型，将视觉-语言-动作（VLA）与生成式潜在世界建模相结合。基于视频的世界动作模型（WAMs）展示了联合未来生成与动作生成对控制的价值，但继承了视频生成器的高昂成本。近期的潜在空间策略避免了像素生成，但通常依赖于中间特征对齐或冻结的目标编码器，将未来预测与VLM的原生特征空间割裂开来。$Z$-sight则在其VLM感知当前场景的视觉标记空间中直接预测未来。通过将前瞻专家和连续动作专家与VLM以混合Transformer架构耦合，$Z$-sight在推理时联合去噪未来空间标记和动作，无需像素重建或外部编码器。在人类视频和机器人轨迹上训练后，$Z$-sight在SIMPLE基准上达到81.9%的成功率（比最强基线高出9.6个百分点），在六项Unitree G1任务上平均成功率为73.3%（高出20.0个百分点），每个块的处理时间为110毫秒，同时在桌面操作基准上保持竞争力。

Authors: Junjie Ye, Yiqi Zhao, Muchen Xu, Celina Shiyu Wang, Hao Dong, Ruohai Ge, Rong Xue, Benjamin J Kolligs, Aditya Dutt, Sasanka Nagavalli, Nassim A. Samad, Gaurav S. Sukhatme, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh, Yue Wang, Yuliang Guo

Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models VLA

world-action model scene structure representation manipulation policy cross-embodiment transfer pretraining data scaling

简要说明：Phoenix 提出了一种用于世界-动作模型的场景结构表示学习方法，通过双教师蒸馏和因果变分自编码器提升操作策略的性能、鲁棒性和跨具身迁移能力。

TLDR: Phoenix introduces a scene-structure representation learning method for world-action models, using dual-teacher distillation and a causal variational autoencoder to improve manipulation policy performance, robustness, and cross-embodiment transfer.

Abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.

摘要（中文）：世界-动作模型联合预测未来的观测与动作，然而，面向重建的视觉表示并未明确强调操作所需的物体空间关系与状态变化。我们提出Phoenix，用于学习场景结构表示以支持世界-动作建模。具体而言，Phoenix编码器通过几何与时空语义知识的双教师蒸馏，丰富DINOv3的通用视觉语义。随后，CS-VAE以因果方式聚合并压缩Phoenix编码器特征为生成式潜变量，同时保留场景信息与空间布局。最后，Phoenix联合预测这些潜变量、互补的外观潜变量以及机器人动作，将场景演化与动作生成联系起来。为研究预训练数据效率，我们整理了约39,000小时的以自我为中心及机器人操作数据用于表示学习，并使用机器人演示子集进行世界-动作模型预训练。在遵循基准特定的后训练流程后，Phoenix在涵盖单臂、双臂及灵巧操作的仿真与真实机器人基准上均取得了最先进性能。其对扰动表现出强大的鲁棒性，在LIBERO-Plus上成功率达94.8%，在RoboTwin 2.0 C2R上达72.4%，同时在Bench2Dex和RoboDojo-RealWorld上分别展现出强跨具身迁移能力与真实世界操作性能。预训练规模分析表明，与仅使用视频VAE的基线相比，数据扩展带来了更大的性能提升，体现出更强的扩展收益与更高效的数据利用。此外，Phoenix在仅使用有限下游演示进行适配时仍保持高成功率，展现了强大的少样本适应能力。我们的代码、预训练数据及模型已在项目页面上公开，以帮助社区复现我们的结果。

Authors: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang, Xiang Li, Yuhang Zheng, Xiaotong Su, Songen Gu, Yichen Zhang, Zebin Xing, Shuai Tian, Jingxiang Guo, Jing Li, Zhiyong Zhao, Zhongpu Xia, Qichao Zhang, Haoran Li, Shuicheng Yan, Dongbin Zhao

Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Manipulation

reward modeling long-horizon manipulation vision-language model open-vocabulary subtasks progress estimation

简要说明：Grana 是一种视觉语言奖励模型，利用开放词汇的子任务描述来估计长时程机器人操作的连续进度，并通过新颖的标注协议和多样化的短时程任务预训练实现零样本泛化。

TLDR: Grana is a vision-language reward model that uses open-vocabulary subtask descriptions to estimate continuous progress for long-horizon robot manipulation, trained with a novel annotation protocol and pretrained on diverse short-horizon tasks for zero-shot generalization.

Abstract: Robot reward modeling faces two challenges: generalizing across tasks and accurately tracking progress in long-horizon manipulation. General-purpose reward models demonstrate broad task transfer, but transfer from short-task pretraining to long-horizon tasks remains underexplored. Long-horizon progress models often rely on task-specific subtask classifiers or fixed action vocabularies, limiting the reuse of learned progress knowledge when adapting to new tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce Grana, a vision-language robot reward model that learns to identify unfinished subtasks and estimate their continuous progress using open-vocabulary subtask descriptions. We train a language-conditioned model to estimate progress in short-horizon tasks and individual subtasks of long-horizon tasks. For long-horizon tasks, we combine the selected subtask's predicted progress with credit for preceding completed subtasks to estimate whole-task progress. General progress prediction requires training the model across diverse tasks with progress supervision that accounts for imperfect execution. Elapsed-time proxies can misrepresent progress when relative subtask durations vary, or failures reverse local progress. We therefore introduce an annotation protocol that converts sparse subtask boundaries and action-quality annotations into dense progress targets, without requiring annotators to assign numerical progress scores. Pretraining with this supervision on 200 diverse, mostly short-horizon manipulation tasks enables zero-shot reward prediction on unseen tasks and improves progress prediction after adaptation to multi-minute, long-horizon tasks. Experiments demonstrate (i) generalizable reward prediction, including adaptation to five long-horizon tasks, (ii) benefits from pretraining and composing subtask progress estimates, and (iii) improved downstream policy performance.

摘要（中文）：机器人奖励建模面临两大挑战：跨任务泛化以及长程操作中进度状态的精确追踪。通用奖励模型展现出广泛的任务迁移能力，但从短任务预训练到长程任务的迁移尚未得到充分探索。长程进度模型通常依赖特定任务的子任务分类器或固定动作词汇表，这限制了在适应新任务时对已学进度知识的复用。为应对上述挑战，我们提出Grana——一种视觉-语言机器人奖励模型，能够识别未完成的子任务，并利用开放词汇的子任务描述估计其连续进度。我们训练了一个语言条件模型，用于估计短程任务及长程任务中各子任务的进度。对于长程任务，我们将选中的子任务预测进度与已完成前序子任务的奖励相结合，以估计整体任务进度。通用进度预测要求模型在多样任务上进行训练，并采用能够反映不完美执行的进度监督。当相对子任务时长变化或失败导致局部进度回退时，基于已用时间的代理指标可能无法准确反映真实进度。为此，我们引入一种标注协议，将稀疏的子任务边界和动作质量标注转换为密集进度目标，而无需标注者为进度赋予数值评分。利用该监督信号在200个多样化、以短程为主的操控任务上进行预训练，使得模型能够对未见任务实现零样本奖励预测，并在适配分钟级长程任务后提升进度预测效果。实验结果表明：(i) 奖励预测具有良好泛化性，包括适配五个长程任务；(ii) 预训练及子任务进度估计的组合带来显著收益；(iii) 下游策略性能得以改善。

Authors: Zi-ang Cao, Kaiyuan Zheng, Yinzhen Xu, Haonan Duan, Jiasheng Gu, Fengyuan Hu, Nan Zhu, Kun Lei, Kevin Lin, Ruijie Zheng, Shenyuan Gao, Fangqi Zhu, Zhe Zhang, Radha Poovendran, Linxi Fan, Guanzhi Wang, Yuke Zhu

DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play Manipulation

diffusion policies world models latent actions human demonstrations reinforcement learning

简要说明：DiWALI 在世界模型中利用从人类和机器人玩耍数据推断的潜在动作来训练扩散策略，减少对动作标签机器人数据的依赖，并在 CALVIN 和真实机器人上通过想象进行策略改进。

TLDR: DiWALI trains diffusion policies for robot manipulation inside a world model using latent actions inferred from human and robot play, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data and enabling policy improvement via imagination on CALVIN and a real robot.

Abstract: Learning robot manipulation is constrained by the availability of action-labeled robot data, for both imitation and world models. Humans can demonstrate skills in seconds, but their demonstrations lack the required robot actions. We introduce DiWALI, a framework that learns and improves diffusion policies within a world model trained on human and robot play. DiWALI infers latent actions from consecutive frames using an inverse dynamics model, enabling world model training without action labels, and grounds them in robot commands through a decoder trained separately on robot play. Skill policies are trained over latent actions from action-free human demonstrations and improved with reinforcement learning in imagination. On the CALVIN benchmark, DiWALI policies trained solely from human demonstrations substantially outperform baselines trained with robot demonstrations. Incorporating human play into the world model training also yields stronger policies after fine-tuning than using the same amount of robot play alone. Experiments on a physical robot show that skills learned primarily from human demonstrations are further improved in imagination with a world model trained on human and robot play. Together, these results demonstrate that human experience can support both manipulation skill acquisition and subsequent policy improvement, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data. Videos, dataset and code are available at https://diwali.cs.uni-freiburg.de.

摘要（中文）：学习机器人操作受到动作标注机器人数据可用性的限制，这一点在模仿学习与世界模型中均有所体现。人类能够在数秒内展示技能，但其演示缺乏所需的机器人动作。我们提出了DiWALI，一个在基于人类与机器人互动数据训练的世界模型中学习并改进扩散策略的框架。DiWALI利用逆动力学模型从连续帧中推断潜在动作，使得无需动作标签即可训练世界模型，并通过单独在机器人互动数据上训练的解码器将这些潜在动作映射为机器人指令。技能策略基于无动作的人类演示中的潜在动作进行训练，并在想象环境中通过强化学习进行改进。在CALVIN基准测试上，仅依靠人类演示训练的DiWALI策略显著优于使用机器人演示训练的基线方法。将人类互动数据纳入世界模型训练后，微调得到的策略也优于单独使用相同数量的机器人互动数据。在实体机器人上的实验表明，主要从人类演示中习得的技能，能够在基于人类与机器人互动数据训练的世界模型中通过想象得到进一步提升。这些结果共同表明，人类经验既能支持操作技能的习得，也能促进后续的策略优化，从而减少对动作标注机器人数据的依赖。相关视频、数据集及代码可在 https://diwali.cs.uni-freiburg.de 获取。

Authors: Akshay L Chandra, Iman Nematollahi, Lingyue Zhao, Daria Kulikova, Angela P. Schoellig, Fabien Despinoy, Abhinav Valada

ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action VLA

Vision-Language-Action memory-augmented VLA latent chain-of-thought manipulation flow-matching action expert

简要说明：ActMem 提出了一种用于 VLA 模型的情境记忆框架，将记忆推理与感知接地解耦，利用潜在记忆思维链条件化流匹配动作专家。在 RoboMemArena、MIKASA-Robo 及真实世界长时程操作任务中取得了最先进的成功率。

TLDR: ActMem introduces an in-context memory framework for VLA models that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding, using a latent Memory Chain-of-Thought to condition a flow-matching action expert. It achieves state-of-the-art success rates on RoboMemArena, MIKASA-Robo, and real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks.

Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in real-world long-horizon manipulation, where memory plays a crucial role. However, existing memory-augmented VLAs either retrieve past observations without reasoning about what they imply, or reason over the full history in a shared context where it crowds out current perception. Cognitive science treats them as distinct systems: memory reconstructs past experience to decide what to do, while perception guides how to act. We therefore propose ActMem, an in-context memory framework that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone. Built on a vision-language model with native video understanding, ActMem infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT), which conditions a flow-matching action expert. Perception Attention further lets the expert attend directly to the current view. To keep inference fast under long histories, Efficient Memory CoT Inference reuses computation across consecutive decisions without changing the output. ActMem achieves 71.1% task success and 80.8% completion success on RoboMemArena, surpassing the strongest baseline by 7.5 and 8.7 percentage points, and 73.8% average success on MIKASA-Robo, the best among all compared methods. In the real world, it reaches 68.8% average success on exogenous, endogenous, and traceless memory tasks, 10.0 percentage points above the strongest memory-augmented VLA. Code and checkpoints will be released at https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem and https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在真实世界长程操控任务中展现出令人鼓舞的性能，而记忆在此类任务中扮演着至关重要的角色。然而，现有的记忆增强型VLA模型要么仅检索过往观测而不对其含义进行推理，要么在共享上下文中对完整历史进行推理，从而挤占了当前感知的处理空间。认知科学将这两者视为不同的系统：记忆重构过往经验以决定做什么，而感知则引导如何行动。为此，我们提出ActMem——一种上下文记忆框架，在单一视觉-语言骨干网络内将记忆推理与感知锚定解耦。ActMem基于具备原生视频理解能力的视觉-语言模型，从带时间戳的交互历史中推断当前子任务，并将此推断过程中形成的隐状态保留为潜在记忆思维链（Memory CoT），用于条件化流匹配动作专家模块。感知注意力机制进一步使专家模块能够直接关注当前视角。为了在长历史条件下保持快速推理，高效记忆思维链推理（Efficient Memory CoT Inference）在连续决策间复用计算资源，且不改变输出结果。ActMem在RoboMemArena基准上达到71.1%的任务成功率和80.8%的完成成功率，分别超越最强基线7.5和8.7个百分点；在MIKASA-Robo基准上取得73.8%的平均成功率，在所有对比方法中表现最佳。在真实世界实验中，ActMem在外源性、内源性和无痕记忆任务上达到68.8%的平均成功率，比最强的记忆增强型VLA高出10.0个百分点。代码和模型权重将发布在 https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem 和 https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem。

Authors: Linfeng Dong, Jianwei Niu, Jiuyi Zhao, Ruibing Feng, Xinghao Wu, Wu Yang, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu, Mu Li

Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation Manipulation

diagnostic benchmark robotic manipulation mind-action composition closed-loop capability attribution

简要说明：Mind2Act World 是一个包含30个模拟机器人操作任务的诊断基准，分别及联合评估基于历史的推理（Mind）、物理执行（Act）及其组合（Mind2Act），揭示最先进的VLA和世界动作模型在单独任务上表现良好，但在闭环组合推理与执行时失败。

TLDR: Mind2Act World is a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated robotic manipulation tasks that separately and jointly evaluate history-based reasoning (Mind), physical execution (Act), and their composition (Mind2Act), revealing that state-of-the-art VLA and world-action models succeed individually but fail when composing reasoning and execution closed-loop.

Abstract: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

摘要（中文）：具身智能旨在让机器人以类人的适应性和可靠性执行复杂的物理任务，这需要三种互补的能力：基于历史的认知推理、精准及时的物理执行，以及通过环境反馈实现推理与执行的组合。然而，现有基准要么在同一任务中同时评估推理与执行，要么分别评估两者而不考察其组合，因此难以揭示失败究竟源于推理、执行，还是二者的组合。我们提出了Mind2Act World，一个包含来自五个真实应用领域的30个模拟操作任务的诊断基准。每个任务设有三个难度级别和两种场景设置（干净场景和随机场景），共形成180种配置。这些任务构成三个视图：Mind测试基于历史观测的决策能力，Act测试精准及时的执行能力，而Mind2Act则在闭环任务中将两者结合，使动作结果指导后续决策。通过对比三个视图，可以判断系统是缺乏某种能力，还是无法组合其已具备的能力。诊断框架进一步将三个代表性系统的失败片段归因于Mind、Act或二者的组合，并以画像卡形式总结每个系统的表现。我们对多模态智能体、视觉-语言-动作模型（VLAs）和世界-动作模型（WAMs）的评估表明，单一视图中的能力并不能迁移到Mind2Act任务中。即使是最强的智能体，在Mind任务中成功率达52.7%，在Act任务中达39.0%，但在Mind2Act任务中仅有12.0%的成功率。最强智能体能够保持任务状态，但在持续接触方面存在困难，而端到端策略能执行已习得的动作，却难以保留任务状态。这些发现表明，通过环境反馈将推理与执行组合起来是当前面临的主要开放性难题。

Authors: Yuzhi Huang, Jie Wu, Fanding Huang, Junchao Lin, Weichen Zhang, Ziyi Xiong, Yang Li, Zhengwei Xie, Zhimin Wang, Zhen Liu, Jiazhen Huang, Yuzheng Zhang, Yuche Liu, Hongyi Yang, Chen Tang, Shixiang Tang, Hakan Aktas, Adam Wu, Duo Wu, Kangye Ji, Shuzhao Xie, Huanan Liu, Weijue Bu, Chenxin Li, Xinyuan Wang, Tianyi Bai, Yinan Mao, Jiawei Wang, Minglei Li, Heng Yu, Ehsan Adeli, Minchen Li, Yong-Lu Li, Cengiz Öztireli, Huazhe Xu, Chao Yu, Jing Zhang, Shanghang Zhang, Weitao Zhou, Wenwu Zhu, Cheng Chi, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang

Beyond the Sink Interpretation: Radial Attention in Flow-Based VLA Policies VLA

flow-based VLA action sink attention analysis token routing π0

简要说明：本文研究基于流的VLA策略中端点动作token的高注意力是否构成'径向动作汇'，发现并非如此；相反，前缀BOS token符合汇特征，且按相对偏移路由动作token可保持性能，表明注意力权重本身不能反映token功能。

TLDR: This paper investigates whether the high attention on endpoint action tokens in a flow-based VLA policy constitutes a 'radial action sink' and finds it does not; instead, the prefix BOS token fits the sink profile, and routing action tokens by relative offsets preserves performance, suggesting attention mass alone is not indicative of token function.

Abstract: Prior work calls the high attention on the first and last action tokens of a flow-based VLA policy a radial action sink, and uses these tokens to set the execution horizon. In language models, a sink is a token with high incoming attention, a small value, and little effect on the output. We test whether that profile holds, not the horizon rule, in one $π_{0.5}$ checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks. The two endpoints receive 5.4% of action-key mass, 1.4 percentage points above their uniform share, and rotary positional encoding produces this excess: directly in shallow layers and through upstream action-token RoPE deeper in the network. The endpoints do not fit the sink profile. Their value norms stay near the action-token mean in all 18 layers. On 250 paired episodes, masking them or zeroing their values changes success by less than 4 points, and replacing their value directions with those of another observation lowers it by 3.2 to 7.2 points across three donors, whereas the same replacement on two non-endpoint tokens in the executed prefix lowers it by 28.4 points. The token that does fit the sink profile on mass and value norm is the prefix BOS; on this checkpoint, zeroing its value raises success in two paired runs, by +13.2 points (95% CI [+7.0, +19.4]) and +6.0 points ([+0.2, +11.8]). Inside the action chunk, a relative-offset routing profile estimated on other tasks keeps 75% of action-token spread and keeps closed-loop success on three held-out tasks (42.7% against a 38.7% baseline), while uniform or shuffled routing drops success to 3-4%. High attention mass alone does not tell what a token does.

摘要（中文）：先前研究将基于流式视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略中动作序列首尾两个动作标记所获得的高注意力关注称为“径向动作汇聚”（radial action sink），并利用这些标记设定执行时域。在语言模型中，“汇聚”（sink）指具有高入向注意力、数值较小且对输出影响甚微的标记。我们检验的是该特征描述是否成立，而非时域规则，具体在五个RoboCasa任务上对一个$π_{0.5}$检查点进行了测试。两个端点标记获得了5.4%的动作键（action-key）注意力质量，比其均匀份额高出1.4个百分点，而旋转位置编码（RoPE）正是产生这一超额注意力的原因：在浅层直接产生作用，并在网络深层通过上游动作标记的RoPE间接影响。端点标记不符合汇聚特征：在全部18层中，其值范数均保持在动作标记均值附近。在250对回合中，掩蔽或置零这些端点的值对成功率的影响不超过4个百分点；而用其他观察值的方向替换其值方向，在三个供体上使成功率降低3.2至7.2个百分点，相比之下，对执行前缀中两个非端点标记进行同样的替换则使成功率降低28.4个百分点。在质量和值范数上符合汇聚特征的是前缀BOS标记；在该检查点上，置零其值在两个配对运行中分别使成功率提高+13.2个百分点（95%置信区间[+7.0， +19.4]）和+6.0个百分点（[+0.2， +11.8]）。在动作块内部，基于其他任务估计的相对偏移路由配置保留了75%的动作标记扩展度，并在三个保留任务上保持了闭环成功率（42.7%，对比基线38.7%），而均匀或随机路由则使成功率骤降至3-4%。仅凭高注意力质量并不能揭示标记的实际功能。

Authors: Yuxi Zheng, Yueqian Lin, Yudong Liu, Zijia Tang, Junyu Pan, Yiheng Wang, Hai Helen Li, Yiran Chen

Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience Manipulation

robot manipulation cross-embodiment skill learning zero-shot transfer heterogeneous interaction

简要说明：UniCraft 通过对齐不同机器人和基准的异构交互数据，联合改进共享操作技能和编排策略，无需演示或权重更新即可零样本迁移到新本体。

TLDR: UniCraft aligns heterogeneous robot interaction data across embodiments and benchmarks to jointly improve a shared manipulation skillset and orchestration policy, demonstrating zero-shot transfer to new embodiments without demonstrations or weight updates.

Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言模型（VLMs）在跨任务和跨领域展示了广泛的泛化能力。然而，在机器人操作中实现同等程度的泛化仍然具有挑战性。机器人本体、任务表述、几何约定及动作接口的异构性，使得跨基准测试和硬件平台上的交互经验呈现碎片化状态。我们通过对齐（alignment）重新思考机器人技能学习：异构的跨基准和跨本体交互能否共同提升一套共享的机器人操作技能？我们提出UniCraft，一个通过对齐异构设置来学习机器人操作技能的框架。具体而言，UniCraft采用一致的坐标约定来表示观测到的场景几何，并对齐不同机器人的感知与控制接口。它将来自不同基准测试的任务组织为规范格式，使得交互反馈能够共同优化共享技能以及引导技能选择与组合的编排策略，而无需任何示范数据或模型权重更新。我们将来自3个基准测试和6种机器人本体的任务交错进行，每种代理模型收集2,700次学习交互。训练过程中，UniCraft在未见场景和任务上的汇总任务成功率分别提升了：LIBERO-PRO上9–28个百分点，RoboTwin 2.0上10.8–13.3个百分点，RoboCasa365（第1–3轮）上3.1–14.4个百分点。训练完成后，在保持所学技能冻结的条件下，UniCraft展示了在robosuite和RoboDojo上的零样本迁移能力，覆盖4种新机器人本体和5种额外的代理模型。

Authors: Ziyue Wang, Yaopeng Yang, Liyi Zhou

Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation Manipulation

long-horizon manipulation agentic robot control event-triggered reasoning task-state monitor efficient token use

简要说明：RoC 是一种用于长时程机器人操作的高效智能体框架，通过任务状态监控器按需触发高级推理，在提升成功率的同时大幅降低令牌消耗。

TLDR: RoC is an efficient agentic framework for long-horizon robot manipulation that uses a task-state monitor to trigger high-level reasoning only when needed, improving success and reducing token use.

Abstract: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

摘要（中文）：大型多模态模型能够支持长时程机器人操作，但频繁调用模型会带来显著的延迟和令牌成本。核心挑战在于判断何时需要智能体辅助或干预，以及错误是否需要修正机器人执行、子任务规划，或两者兼而有之。为解决这一问题，我们提出了RoC（按需推理）框架，一种高效框架，通过在线任务状态监控器协调低层策略与高层推理智能体。该监控器将时序视觉观测与有序交互记忆相结合，共同估计当前子任务内的进展并预测其后续子任务。这些预测引导事件触发的智能体审查，以实现协同的执行修复与规划修订。验证结果用于管理记忆更新与子任务转换，使得常规执行由策略负责，而推理则聚焦于需要额外评估的决策。在RMBench上，RoC相比最强的基于智能体的基线，任务成功率提升了24.0个百分点，同时令牌消耗减少了65.3%。在任务成功率方面，它也优于最强的基于策略的基线，高出15.1个百分点。真实世界实验进一步验证了其在三项长时程操作任务中的有效性。总体而言，RoC支持高效智能体干预以及跨执行与规划维度的协同恢复，适用于长时程机器人操作。

Authors: Zilang Cen, Chao Tang, Fangcheng Liu, Weishi Mi, Wei Hao, JiaYu Xu, Dehao Huang, Yehui Tang, Xiaohui Cui, Tingguang Li, Xiaoyuan Zhang

FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving AutonomousDriving

vision-language-action off-road autonomous driving action buffer motion-conditioned execution inference efficiency

简要说明：FastRoverVLA 提出了一种无需训练的接口，将视觉-语言-动作（VLA）规划生成与基于运动状态的执行解耦，通过速度-曲率动作缓冲区和有界刷新规则，在降低推理成本的同时提升越野自动驾驶轨迹精度。

TLDR: FastRoverVLA introduces a training-free interface that decouples vision-language-action (VLA) plan generation from motion-conditioned execution, using a speed-curvature action buffer and a bounded refresh rule to reduce inference costs while improving trajectory accuracy for off-road autonomous driving.

Abstract: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion at each update, integrated into a local trajectory, and advanced by consuming the current action. The corrected remainder is written back to the buffer, preserving motion corrections across successive updates. A bounded refresh rule normalizes speed and curvature variations within a newly decoded plan and assigns a short or long reuse budget according to the resulting plan-roughness score. The interface requires neither backbone features nor an additional learned driving policy. Over a 3 s horizon, independent real-request evaluation achieves average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) of 0.328/0.596 m on ORAD-3D and 0.266/0.526 m on RELLIS-3D, reducing FDE by 18.0% and 36.7% at request rates of 6.0% and 4.8%, respectively. These runs retain lower errors across four backbones and both datasets and reduce Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by factors of 16.6 and 20.8 under serial replay, while mechanism and motion-only controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the observed accuracy benefit. The source code and evaluation materials are publicly available at https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA.

摘要（中文）：越野视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型能够生成基于场景条件的规划轨迹，但频繁的轨迹更新会反复触发昂贵的多模态推理调用。复用预测结果可降低这一计算需求，但复用后的指令可能无法适应车辆运动状态的变化。FastRoverVLA通过将视觉规划生成与运动条件执行解耦，解决了这一不匹配问题。其免训练接口在视觉预测之间保持已解码的规划轨迹。在每个更新周期，一个速度-曲率动作缓冲区与实测运动状态对齐，集成至局部轨迹中，并通过消耗当前动作向前推进。修正后的剩余轨迹被写回缓冲区，从而在连续更新之间保留运动修正信息。一个有界的刷新规则对最新解码规划中的速度与曲率变化进行归一化处理，并根据计算得到的规划粗糙度评分分配短或长的复用预算。该接口既不需要骨干网络特征，也不依赖额外学习的驾驶策略。在3秒预测时域内，独立真实请求评估在ORAD-3D数据集上实现了平均位移误差（ADE）和最终位移误差（FDE）分别为0.328/0.596米，在RELLIS-3D数据集上分别为0.266/0.526米，在请求率分别为6.0%和4.8%时，FDE分别降低了18.0%和36.7%。这些运行在四种骨干网络和两个数据集上均保持了更低的误差，并在串行复用模式下将Qwen3-VL请求处理成本分别降低了16.6倍和20.8倍。机制消融与仅运动控制实验表明，持续状态修正观测到的精度提升的主要来源。源代码和评估材料已在 https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA 公开提供。

Authors: Changtao Zhao, Yingxue Guan, Li Wang, Shijie Zhao, Yuhang Zhang, Shengkai Zhang, Qing Wang, Ziying Song

EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL VLA

post-training robot-use agent distillation reinforcement learning LIBERO

简要说明：EmbodyAgent 提出了一种完整的后训练流程（黑盒蒸馏、SFT 和在线 RL），将开源的 9B VLM 转变为在 LIBERO Spatial 任务上高性能的具身智能体，将保留成功率从 0/100 提升至 84/100。

TLDR: EmbodyAgent presents a full post-training pipeline (black-box distillation, SFT, and online RL) that turns an open-weight 9B VLM into a high-performing embodied agent for LIBERO Spatial tasks, improving held-out success from 0/100 to 84/100.

Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言模型（VLMs）可作为闭环机器人使用智能体（RUAs），通过工具接口编写并执行控制代码。然而，将开源权重的VLM转化为高性能具身智能体，需要一套完整的后训练栈：开箱即用的开源VLM在交互式工具契约上完全失效；强大的前沿教师模型仅以黑盒端点形式可访问，不暴露权重或词元概率；而仅靠有监督模仿在 rollout 分布偏移下性能趋于平台期。我们提出 **EmbodyAgent**，一个端到端后训练框架，包含三条紧密耦合的流水线：（1）**黑盒数据合成流水线**，在强制的“先思考后编码”契约下查询强教师模型，并根据任务成功与否筛选轨迹；（2）**SFT流水线**，将解释与程序目标蒸馏进一个开源9B VLM，视觉与语言编码器均可训练；（3）**在线强化学习流水线**，通过组相对优势（group-relative advantage）并结合运行时错误惩罚的结果奖励，优化学生生成的回合数据。三条流水线共享同一个无原语Python执行工具，仅暴露原始视觉观测与七维末端执行器控制，无动作解码器，跨阶段接口不变。在十个LIBERO Spatial任务上的严格分离评测协议（状态划分不重叠、测试时贪心解码、训练专用安全防护）下，100个测试状态上的保留成功率从0/100（基础9B VLM）提升至14/100（SFT之后），再提升至84/100（RL之后）；训练rollout成功率从8.4%攀升至87.7%，每个回合的中位模型调用次数从36次降至11次。我们进一步识别出基于结果奖励的可执行代码RL所引发的自强化运行时错误模式，并建立失败类别监控与采样侧筛选协议，以稳定训练过程。

One View, One Action: Spatially Generalizable VLAs through Observation-Aligned Experts and Cross Graph Consistency VLA

multi-view VLA spatial generalization cross-graph consistency manipulation policy observation-aligned experts

简要说明：OVOA-VLA通过在每相机的坐标系中预测动作，并联合训练基础框架专家和视图特定专家以及跨图一致性，提高了多视图VLA模型在空间泛化上的能力，在LIBERO和真实机器人操作中取得更好表现。

TLDR: OVOA-VLA improves spatial generalization of multi-view VLA models by predicting actions in each camera frame, training base-frame and view-specific experts with directed attention graphs and cross-graph consistency. It achieves higher success rates on LIBERO and real-world manipulation under camera and initial-state perturbations.

Abstract: Multi-view vision-language-action (VLA) models still face challenges in spatial generalization, particularly under changes in camera viewpoints and robot initial states. These models typically receive action supervision only in the robot base frame, requiring them to implicitly learn the spatial correspondence between observations from each view and base-frame actions. We propose One View, One Action (OVOA-VLA), which learns to predict actions in each view's camera frame, allowing the same physical motion to provide diverse, observation-aligned supervision across views. OVOA-VLA jointly trains a base-frame expert and view-specific action experts, whose robot-state inputs and action targets are expressed in their respective camera frames. Two complementary directed attention graphs model both directions of interaction between the base and view-specific experts, jointly leveraging view-specific action supervision to improve base-frame prediction. Cross Graph Consistency further encourages agreement between the two graphs' base-frame predictions for the same sample. With the same multi-view inputs, the model supports both full and base-only inference. Experiments across multiple simulation benchmarks demonstrate improved manipulation performance and robustness to camera-viewpoint and robot-initialization perturbations. Full and base-only inference achieve average success rates of 88.1% and 85.7% on LIBERO-Plus, respectively. In real-world evaluations, base-only inference raises the average success rates from $π_{0.5}$'s 28.3% to 58.3% across three tasks under spatial distribution shifts.

摘要（中文）：多视角视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在空间泛化方面仍面临挑战，尤其是在相机视点和机器人初始状态发生变化的情况下。这类模型通常仅在机器人基座坐标系中接收动作监督，需要隐式地学习每个视角观测与基座坐标系动作之间的空间对应关系。我们提出“一视角一动作”（OVOA-VLA）方法，该方法学习在每个视角的相机坐标系中预测动作，从而使相同的物理运动能够为不同视角提供多样化且与观测对齐的监督信号。OVOA-VLA联合训练一个基座坐标系专家和多个视角专用动作专家，其机器人状态输入和动作目标均在各目的相机坐标系中表达。两个互补的有向注意力图分别建模基座专家与视角专用专家之间的双向交互，联合利用视角专用动作监督来提升基座坐标系预测的准确性。跨图一致性机制进一步促使两个图对同一样本的基座坐标系预测结果保持一致。在相同的多视角输入条件下，该模型同时支持完整推理和仅基座推理。在多个仿真基准上的实验表明，该方法在操控性能和对抗相机视点及机器人初始化扰动的鲁棒性方面均有显著提升。在LIBERO-Plus基准上，完整推理和仅基座推理的平均成功率分别达到88.1%和85.7%。在真实世界评估中，面对空间分布偏移，仅基座推理在三个任务上将平均成功率从π₀.₅的28.3%提升至58.3%。

Authors: Jinxi Liu, Ruifeng Zhai, Hao Liu, Guangrun Wang

PhysVAM: Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation Manipulation

future-value prediction dynamic object manipulation action generation gated cross-attention task progress

简要说明：PhysVAM 是一种面向物理学的未来价值动作模型，通过预测多个时间范围的任务进展来引导动态物体操作中的动作生成，在仿真和真实世界任务中取得了显著的成功率提升。

TLDR: PhysVAM is a physics-oriented future value action model that predicts task progress across multiple horizons to guide action generation for dynamic object manipulation, achieving significant success-rate improvements in simulation and real-world tasks.

Abstract: Predicting future scene or object states does not necessarily reveal how robot-object interactions will advance or hinder a task. This challenge is particularly pronounced in dynamic robotic manipulation, where objects continue moving during perception and execution. Effective action generation therefore requires not only modeling object dynamics but also anticipating how future interactions will shape task progress. To this end, we propose \textbf{PhysVAM}, a Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model that represents anticipated interactions through their effects on future task progress. This value-based formulation provides task-directed foresight without reconstructing future visual states. Conditioned on current observations and historical object and robot motion, PhysVAM jointly learns action generation and multi-horizon future-value prediction. The value branch learns horizon-specific latent representations through future task-value prediction from successful and failed trajectories. These future-value representations are integrated into the action policy through gated cross-attention, guiding action generation toward interactions that facilitate task success. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate superior task success, with absolute success-rate improvements of 27.0 and 27.5 percentage points over the strongest baselines in simulation and real-world tasks, respectively. Project page: https://metarobo.github.io/physvam.github.io/.

摘要（中文）：预测未来场景或物体状态，并不一定能揭示机器人-物体交互将如何推进或阻碍任务进展。这一挑战在动态机器人操作中尤为突出，因为物体在感知和执行过程中持续运动。因此，有效的动作生成不仅需要对物体动力学进行建模，还需要预判未来交互将如何影响任务进展。为此，我们提出了\textbf{PhysVAM}，一种面向物理学的未来价值动作模型，通过未来任务进展的影响来表征预期的交互。这种基于价值的表述提供了面向任务的前瞻性，而无需重建未来的视觉状态。基于当前观测以及历史物体和机器人运动，PhysVAM联合学习动作生成与多时间跨度未来价值预测。价值分支通过从成功和失败轨迹中进行未来任务价值预测，学习时间跨度特定的潜在表征。这些未来价值表征通过门控交叉注意力机制整合到动作策略中，引导动作生成朝向促进任务成功的交互方向发展。大量的仿真和真实世界实验证明了其卓越的任务成功率，在仿真和真实世界任务中，相较于最强基线，绝对成功率分别提升了27.0和27.5个百分点。项目页面：https://metarobo.github.io/physvam.github.io/。

Authors: Yuxiang Yang, Jingbo Zhang, Jiaru Zhong, Junliang Chen, Yirui Zhou, Guangming Wang, Haitao Lin, Huaiyuan Xu, Yi Wang, Lap-Pui Chau

Dynamic Human-Robot Role Allocation through Entropy-Based Monitoring and LLM Reasoning Manipulation

human-robot collaboration role allocation entropy-based monitoring LLM reasoning behavior tree

简要说明：本文提出一种人机协作框架，通过基于熵的手-物交互监测和LLM偏好提取，动态分配机器人角色，让人自由行动，并能在异常时触发机器人纠错。

TLDR: This paper presents a human-robot collaboration framework that uses entropy-based monitoring of hand-object interactions and LLM-based preference extraction to dynamically allocate roles to a robot, leaving the human free to act, with anomaly-triggered corrective robot actions.

Abstract: Role allocation strategies in human-robot collaboration typically assign tasks to both the human and the robot, limiting the user's ability to take initiative. Furthermore, allocation decisions may conflict with the user's intentions, and the rationale behind such allocations may remain unclear, potentially reducing both acceptance and collaboration fluency. The novelty of the proposed framework is that the human is left free to contribute to the task, while the robot is dynamically allocated activities through a cost-driven Behavior Tree architecture according to user-expressed preferences and behavior. Explicit preferences are extracted from natural language instructions using a large language model, whereas human activity is monitored online through a Shannon entropy-based analysis of hand-object interactions. Furthermore, the framework can recognize anomalies in human execution and autonomously trigger corrective robot actions. The approach was validated through a pilot study and a multi-subject experiment involving 14 participants. Results demonstrate the potential of such an allocation strategy for enabling intuitive and engaging collaboration without increasing the perceived workload.

摘要（中文）：人机协作中的任务分配策略通常会将任务同时分配给人和机器人，这限制了用户主动性的发挥。此外，分配决策可能与用户意图相冲突，且此类分配背后的逻辑依据可能不明确，从而可能降低接受度和协作流畅性。所提出框架的新颖之处在于，人类可自由参与任务，而机器人则通过一种成本驱动的行为树架构，根据用户表达的偏好和行为被动态分配活动。显式偏好通过大语言模型从自然语言指令中提取，而人类活动则通过基于香农熵的手-物交互分析进行在线监测。此外，该框架能够识别人类执行过程中的异常，并自主触发机器人的纠正动作。该方法通过一项先导研究和一项涉及14名参与者的多受试者实验进行了验证。结果表明，这种分配策略在不增加感知工作负荷的情况下，具有实现直观且引人入胜的协作的潜力。

Authors: Elena Merlo, Marta Lagomarsino, Hamidreza Raei, Arash Ajoudani

Reference-Free Humanoid Skateboarding via Termination-Shaped Reinforcement Learning HumanoidEmbodied

humanoid skateboarding model-free reinforcement learning termination-shaped rewards object-mediated locomotion K1 humanoid

简要说明：该论文提出了一种无模型深度强化学习框架，利用阻止利用的终止条件，使K1人形机器人无需演示或解析转向模型即可学习滑板，从姿态控制逐步过渡到持续的机器人-滑板运动。

TLDR: The paper introduces a model-free deep reinforcement learning framework with exploit-blocking terminations that enables a K1 humanoid robot to learn skateboarding without demonstrations or analytic steering models, progressing from stance control to sustained robot-board locomotion.

Abstract: Humanoid locomotion research has advanced rapidly on walking and running, but \emph {object-mediated} locomotion, in which a robot must coordinate its body with a passive external object, remains difficult. One challenging task is skateboarding, which requires simultaneous interaction with the ground and a passive but movable platform to achieve forward motion. Current methods for tackling skateboarding with humanoid robots either require human demonstrations or utilise analytic steering models that require system identification. In this paper, we introduce a deep reinforcement learning framework that does not rely on prior data such as demonstrations and enables robots such as the K1 humanoid to learn to skateboard using model-free learning. The method combines task rewards with exploit-blocking terminations. We introduce a number of constraints restricting behaviours such as losing the planted board foot, standing with both feet on the board, excessive twisting, separation from the board, and unstable board motion. Their changing prevalence during training produces an implicit progression from stance control towards sustained robot--board locomotion.

摘要（中文）：仿人机器人运动研究在行走与跑步方面已取得快速进展，但涉及机器人必须协调自身与被动外部物体的“物体中介”运动仍具挑战性。其中一项难题是滑板运动，这要求机器人同时与地面及被动但可移动的平台交互，以实现向前移动。当前应对仿人机器人滑板运动的方法要么依赖人类演示，要么利用需要系统辨识的解析转向模型。本文提出一种深度强化学习框架，该框架不依赖演示等先验数据，使K1仿人机器人等能够通过无模型学习学会滑板技巧。该方法将任务奖励与利用阻断终止相结合，并引入多项约束以限制诸如失去踩板脚、双脚站立于板上、过度扭转、与板分离及板运动不稳定等行为。训练过程中这些约束的占比变化，自然形成了从姿态控制向持续性人—板运动的渐进式过渡。

Authors: Ganeshvar Soenessardien, Michael Przystupa, Kevin Sebastian Luck

Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models WorldModel

world models action-conditioned video prediction action perturbation policy evaluation model-based planning

简要说明：本文提出AFFECT，一种用于世界模型的辅助目标，通过匹配注入动作噪声引起的视觉变化分布，使世界模型对动作扰动的响应更忠实，从而改进真实机器人上的策略评估和规划。

TLDR: This paper proposes AFFECT, an auxiliary objective for world models that makes them more faithful to action perturbations by matching the distribution of visual changes induced by injected action noise, improving policy evaluation and planning on real robots.

Abstract: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. Yet despite producing increasingly realistic videos, current world models often fail to capture how small action changes affect future observations. This limits their use in tasks such as robotic policy evaluation and model-based planning, where nearly identical actions can lead to qualitatively different outcomes. To address this, we propose AFFECT, an auxiliary training objective for learning the distribution of visual changes induced by action perturbations. Specifically, we inject temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation. We then train the world model so that its generated videos respond to this noise as the recorded videos do, without requiring repeated executions from the same initial state. Across OGBench simulation and real-world DROID and ALOHA-2 setups, AFFECT makes world-model rollouts more faithful to real outcomes. On DROID, the Pearson correlation between policy success rates in the world model and on the real robot rises from 0.47 to 0.79, alongside up to 23% lower FVD. These gains carry over to planning, where selecting actions with AFFECT-trained world models improves task success by up to 8.3%.

摘要（中文）：世界模型旨在预测动作作用下的环境动态，从而无需在现实世界中实际执行动作即可预测其结果。然而，尽管当前的世界模型能够生成越来越逼真的视频，它们却常常无法捕捉到细微动作变化对未来观测的影响。这限制了它们在机器人策略评估和基于模型的规划等任务中的应用，在这些任务中，几乎相同的动作可能导致截然不同的结果。为解决这一问题，我们提出了AFFECT，一种用于学习动作扰动所引发的视觉变化分布的辅助训练目标。具体而言，我们向基于与任务无关的人类遥操作训练的策略中注入时间相关的噪声。随后，我们训练世界模型，使其生成的视频对噪声的响应方式与记录的视频一致，而无需从相同的初始状态进行重复执行。在OGBench仿真以及真实世界的DROID和ALOHA-2平台上，AFFECT使世界模型的滚动预测更贴近真实结果。在DROID上，世界模型与真实机器人中策略成功率之间的皮尔逊相关系数从0.47提升至0.79，同时FVD最多降低23%。这些提升同样延伸至规划任务中，使用经AFFECT训练的世界模型进行动作选择，可将任务成功率最高提升8.3%。

Authors: John Won, Yonghoon Dong, Jinwoo Shin

Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion Locomotion

quadruped locomotion gait selection deep reinforcement learning central pattern generators terrain adaptation

简要说明：该论文利用深度强化学习和振荡器网络学习11种四足步态及一个门控策略，该策略根据地形、性能指标和速度选择最佳步态，并展示了零样本泛化到新地形、新步态和更大四足机器人的能力。

TLDR: This paper uses deep reinforcement learning and oscillator networks to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits and a gating policy that selects the optimal gait for a given terrain, performance metric, and velocity, demonstrating zero-shot generalization to new terrains, gaits, and larger quadrupeds.

Abstract: Animals use many different gaits to locomote at different speeds across varying terrains. A longstanding question in biology and robotics is: which gait is best? This question is most often addressed from an energy-efficiency perspective on flat terrain, leaving open how the answer depends on terrain and on the criterion optimized. Here we show that gait optimality is determined jointly by terrain, performance metric, and velocity. We use deep reinforcement learning and networks of abstract oscillators, modeling spinal central pattern generators, to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits across diverse challenging terrains, together with the locomotion style (base height, foot ground clearance, foot offsets) that each requires. A second policy then selects among them to optimize a user-specified criterion such as cost of transport, base stability, or joint smoothness. Across these performance metrics and within this repertoire, every gait is optimal under at least one terrain-metric-velocity combination. The framework adapts zero-shot to gait couplings and styles never seen during training, to terrains far beyond the training distribution, and to larger quadrupeds five times the training mass. With a single additional pitch-tracking reward term, the same gait couplings also support bipedal-mode locomotion. Our method provides a general and systematic way to produce expressive locomotion and to select the gait best suited to a given terrain and criterion. Project page: https://guillaume10.github.io/terrain-gaits.

摘要（中文）：动物在不同地形上以不同速度移动时，会采用多种步态。生物学和机器人学中一个长期存在的问题是：哪种步态最优？这个问题通常从平坦地形上的能量效率角度来探讨，但尚未明确答案如何依赖于地形以及所优化的标准。在此，我们证明步态的优越性由地形、性能指标和速度共同决定。我们使用深度强化学习和抽象振荡器网络（模拟脊髓中央模式发生器）来学习跨越多种挑战性地形的11种四足步态，以及每种步态所需的运动风格（身体高度、足部离地间隙、足部偏移）。随后，第二个策略从中进行选择，以优化用户指定的标准，如运输成本、身体稳定性或关节平滑度。在这些性能指标和这一步态库内，每种步态至少在一种地形-指标-速度组合下是最优的。该框架能够零样本适应训练中从未见过的步态耦合和风格，适应远超训练分布的地形，以及适应质量为训练质量五倍的更大四足动物。仅需增加一个俯仰跟踪奖励项，相同的步态耦合也能支持双足模式运动。我们的方法提供了一种通用且系统化的方式，以生成富有表现力的运动，并选择最适合特定地形和标准的步态。项目页面：https://guillaume10.github.io/terrain-gaits。

Authors: Guillaume Bellegarda, Auke Ijspeert

Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models WorldModel

latent world model model predictive planning success-latency trade-off goal-directed planning benchmark

简要说明：Fast-JEPA 提出了一种潜在世界模型规划框架，通过预测完整候选结果和使用目标导向计划来加速动作序列搜索，在多个控制基准上以更低延迟实现更高成功率。

TLDR: Fast-JEPA proposes a latent world model planning framework that accelerates action-sequence search by predicting complete candidate outcomes and using goal-directed plans, achieving higher success rates with lower latency across several control benchmarks.

Abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our code is available at https://github.com/Sofilyzia/Fast-JEPA.

摘要（中文）：潜在世界模型能够预测动作序列的结果，但在测试阶段通过递归展开来比较候选规划仍然代价高昂。我们提出了Fast-JEPA，一种潜在世界模型规划框架，它推进了预测搜索在成功率-延迟帕累托前沿上的表现。Fast-JEPA重新组织预测计算，以支持在低规划成本下进行有效的动作序列搜索。它构建目标导向的规划来引导搜索，并直接预测完整候选序列的结果以实现高效比较，从而避免在细化过程中进行递归状态展开。在PushT、Reacher、Cube和TwoRoom任务中，Fast-JEPA实现了96.50%的平均成功率，且规划速度比INTACT快2.41倍。搜索预算扫描表明，其具有竞争力的成功率和低延迟在候选数量及细化深度变化时依然保持。我们进一步引入了DynaGoal，这是一个用于在动态分布外条件、执行期限和受控响应延迟下评估世界模型规划的基准。Fast-JEPA在DynaGoal-Shift上实现了73.83%的平均成功率，在DynaGoal-Deadline上实现了87.67%的平均成功率，展示了在变化的控制条件和执行时间约束下低延迟预测规划的实用价值。我们的代码可在https://github.com/Sofilyzia/Fast-JEPA获取。

Authors: Yao Zhang, Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Haishan Liu, Changti Wu, Yu Wu, Kai Chen

ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control HumanoidEmbodied

in-context learning whole-body control humanoid robot behavior foundation model residual adaptation

简要说明：ECHO提出了一种用于人形机器人全身控制的上下文行为基础模型，将通用行为能力和特定动力学执行分离，通过上下文表示和残差适配实现环境特定控制而无需测试时参数更新，并在Unitree G1上展示了全身遥操作和负载适配。

TLDR: ECHO introduces an in-context behavior foundation model for humanoid whole-body control that separates general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution, using context representation and residual adaptation to enable environment-specific control without test-time parameter updates, with deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrating whole-body teleoperation and payload adaptation.

Abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

摘要（中文）：类人行为基础模型（BFMs）通过大规模运动模仿和大规模并行强化学习获得多样化技能，然而广泛的行为能力并不能确保在不同物理条件下实现精确执行。若不区分潜在动力学特性，策略可能会偏向于保守的折中方案，而非针对特定环境实现精准控制。我们提出ECHO，一种上下文行为基础模型，将交互经验转化为环境特定的控制能力，将通用行为能力与动力学特定执行相分离。混合与退火采样（Mixed and Annealed Sampling）首先通过平衡针对性练习与广泛运动覆盖，在单一预训练阶段建立行为先验。在此先验基础上，上下文表示与残差自适应（Context Representation and Residual Adaptation）从交互历史中学习结构化动力学表示，以指导对冻结先验的残差修正，从而实现无需测试时参数更新的自适应。大量实验表明，ECHO在多样运动与物理条件下均优于所有基线方法。此外，在Unitree G1上的部署展示了涵盖极限杂技与地形交互的全身遥操作，以及在操作任务和全身控制中的载荷自适应能力。项目页面见 https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

Authors: Xingyi Wang, Bin Li, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Weiji Xie, Xiangyu Miao, Junsong Wu, Wei Song, Shiqiang Zhu, Chenjia Bai

Hindsight Self-Distillation: Teaching Robots to Act from the Present Manipulation

self-distillation visual summaries denoising robot manipulation action prediction

简要说明：HSD 利用事后帧通过自蒸馏训练机器人策略，使学生在当前图像上预测动作，在 LIBERO 和 RoboTwin 上取得高成功率。

TLDR: HSD trains robots by self-distillation from hindsight, using later demonstration frames to teach a student policy to predict actions from current images, achieving high success on LIBERO and RoboTwin.

Abstract: A robot must choose an action before it can see the outcome. In a recorded demonstration, later camera frames show what happened after the robot moved. Hindsight Self-Distillation (HSD) uses these later frames to teach a policy what to extract from current images. During training, a teacher sees both the current and later frames, while a student sees the current frames. They share a visual encoder and an action predictor. Each branch summarizes its images with a small set of feature vectors. These visual summaries supply all visual input to the action predictor. The teacher learns from demonstrated actions. For each noisy action sequence, the student learns from either the demonstration or the teacher's denoising prediction. It also learns to match the teacher's visual summaries. We analyze which aspects of the teacher's predictions the student can recover from its inputs. At deployment, the student encodes the current images once and reuses its summaries at every denoising step. HSD achieves average success rates of 98.50\% on LIBERO and 92.31\% on RoboTwin 2.0.

摘要（中文）：机器人必须在看到结果之前选择动作。在录制的演示中，后续的摄像头帧展示了机器人移动后发生的情况。后见之明自蒸馏（HSD）利用这些后续帧，教导策略从当前图像中提取何种信息。在训练过程中，教师模型同时看到当前帧和后续帧，而学生模型仅看到当前帧。两者共享视觉编码器和动作预测器。每个分支通过一小组特征向量对其图像进行概括。这些视觉摘要为动作预测器提供全部视觉输入。教师模型从演示动作中学习。对于每个含噪声的动作序列，学生模型从演示或教师模型的去噪预测中学习，同时学习匹配教师模型的视觉摘要。我们分析了学生模型能从其输入中恢复教师模型预测的哪些方面。在部署时，学生模型仅需对当前图像编码一次，并在每个去噪步骤中重复使用其摘要。HSD在LIBERO上实现了98.50%的平均成功率，在RoboTwin 2.0上实现了92.31%的平均成功率。

Authors: Haisen He, Yechi Liu, Tianle Shi, Haoyun Liu, Chuanzhang Meng, Tiancai Jiao, Yifan Bai, Xinyuan Chang, SongLin Dong, Zhiheng Ma

TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation Manipulation

vision-tactile-language-action dexterous manipulation illumination robustness action reliability tactile feedback

简要说明：TipDex-VTLA 提出了一种视觉-触觉-语言-动作策略，通过视觉可靠性估计和触觉预测验证来决定何时优化动作，从而在未见过的光照条件下提升灵巧操作的成功率。

TLDR: TipDex-VTLA introduces a vision-tactile-language-action policy that uses visual reliability estimation and tactile forecast verification to decide when to refine actions, improving dexterous manipulation under unseen lighting conditions.

Abstract: Changes in illumination can induce action drift in dexterous manipulation even when the physical state remains unchanged. Although existing vision--tactile--language--action (VTLA) policies incorporate tactile feedback, when and how touch refines actions under changing visual conditions remains challenging. We introduce \textbf{TipDex-VTLA}, a VTLA policy that combines estimated visual action reliability and tactile forecast verification to regulate execution-time refinement. Specifically, Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) learns visual reliability from a frozen reference policy's action sensitivity to illumination perturbations. Tactile Anticipation and Correction during Execution (TACE) compares predicted and measured touch at matched times and combines the resulting discrepancy with visual reliability to gate bounded feature corrections for unexecuted actions. This effectively helps to refine actions under challenging unseen visual conditions. We evaluate TipDex-VTLA on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks and the UniVTAC simulation benchmark. TipDex-VTLA trained on data collected under normal visual conditions, achieves average full-task success rates of 87.5% (resp. 73.8%) under normal (resp. challenging unseen) lighting in real-world tasks, significantly outperforming some state-of-the-art methods. We will release the collected data and source code.

摘要（中文）：光照变化即使在物理状态保持不变的情况下，也可能导致灵巧操作中的动作漂移。尽管现有的视觉-触觉-语言-动作（VTLA）策略整合了触觉反馈，但在视觉条件变化时，触觉何时以及如何优化动作仍是一个挑战。我们提出了\textbf{TipDex-VTLA}，一种结合估计的视觉动作可靠性与触觉预测验证来调节执行时优化的VTLA策略。具体而言，视觉动作敏感性估计（VASE）通过冻结参考策略的动作对光照扰动的敏感性来学习视觉可靠性；执行期间触觉预测与校正（TACE）在匹配时刻比较预测与实测的触觉信息，并将所得差异与视觉可靠性相结合，对未执行动作进行有界的特征校正。这有效地帮助在具有挑战性的未知视觉条件下优化动作。我们在四个真实世界灵巧操作任务和UniVTAC仿真基准上评估了TipDex-VTLA。在正常视觉条件下收集的数据上训练的TipDex-VTLA，在真实世界任务中，正常（分别具有挑战性的未知）光照条件下的平均完整任务成功率达87.5%（分别73.8%），显著优于若干最先进的方法。我们将公开所收集的数据和源代码。

Authors: Xudi Ge, Yepeng Liu, Haifeng Liu, Enze Shi, Liangqi Zhang, Yongchao Xu

CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control VLA

causal latent world model asynchronous control flow matching LIBERO-10 vision-language-action

简要说明：CauSyncVLA 提出一种异步双系统 VLA 控制器，利用因果潜在世界模型预测过期的感知记忆，并通过流程预热启动进行轨迹校正，在 LIBERO-10 上提升了闭环鲁棒性和推理吞吐量。

TLDR: CauSyncVLA introduces an asynchronous dual-system VLA controller using a causal latent world model to predict stale perceptual memory and a flow warm-starting mechanism for trajectory correction, improving closed-loop robustness and inference throughput on LIBERO-10.

Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略必须在视觉推理仍在进行时做出反应。计算与执行的重叠减少了等待时间，却导致感知记忆过时，且连续的动作片段之间缺乏衔接。我们提出了CauSyncVLA，一种异步双系统控制器，它将感知记忆预测和轨迹修正与实际机器人执行相对齐。不同于预测像素或物理状态，因果潜在世界模型从延迟的视觉锚点和已执行的状态-动作历史中预测当前的感知记忆，并通过动作敏感蒸馏进行监督，以保留冻结专家模型的控制响应。在此更新的记忆条件下，预测流预热启动（PFWS）将未执行的动作视界对齐，以进行单步流修正，且无需额外训练。在LIBERO-10基准上，CauSyncVLA以5.04倍的推理吞吐量达到了93.8%的成功率，提升了闭环鲁棒性和机器人运动平滑度。
